---
title: "Bias Correction of GFDL-MOM6-COBALT2 Ocean Temperature (thetao)"
subtitle: "Eastern Scotian Shelf — using pre-extracted WOA/GFDL climatologies"
output: html_document
---

## Overview

**Purpose:** Correct monthly GFDL temperature at 9 depths (1961–2010) so that
its 1981–2010 monthly climatology matches the World Ocean Atlas (WOA).

**Method:**

1. Load the pre-extracted, per-depth WOA and GFDL monthly climatologies
   (1981–2010) and compute their regional (cos-lat weighted) means.
2. Bias = WOA climatology − GFDL climatology, per depth × calendar month
   (108 values = 9 depths × 12 months).
3. Extract the raw monthly GFDL series (1961–2010) from the zarr store and
   compute its regional monthly mean.
4. Corrected value = GFDL value + bias (same offset every year, so GFDL's
   interannual variability and trend are preserved).
5. Average to annual means (only years with 12 valid months).

<!--
6. Splice in the bias-corrected ISIMIP3b projection (2015–2100), with a
   linear gap fill for 2011–2014.
   (Not implemented in this file.)
-->

**LIMITATION — this correction fixes the LEVEL, not the TREND (added 2026-10-08).**

Step 2 builds the bias from `woa_temp_all-depths_monthly.csv`, which is a
**climatology** (depth × calendar month, no year axis). A single additive
offset per depth × month therefore cannot alter the slope: GFDL's own trend is
inherited unchanged, exactly as step 4 states. That is correct as implemented,
but it means any error in GFDL's *rate* of warming survives the correction.

Measured on the output of this script (`Ocean_temp_by_Depth_1961_2100.csv`):

| window | r0to50 | r50to150 | surface − deep gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1961–2024 | +0.264 °C/dec | +0.213 °C/dec | widens, +0.051/dec (p = 0.029) |
| 1993–2023 | +0.495 °C/dec | +0.378 °C/dec | widens, +0.116/dec |

Observations for this shelf show the OPPOSITE vertical structure. Zhai et al.
(2025, Copernicus Ocean State Report 9, State Planet 6-osr9/5,
doi:10.5194/sp-6-osr9-5-2025) report from GLORYS12V1 validated against AZMP
moorings that "the bottom temperature shows a stronger increasing trend than
the SST", and that after 2012 "the annual bottom temperature became higher
than the annual SST", with a regime shift around 2012. In this forcing the deep
layer never exceeds the surface at any point 1961–2100, and the gap widens
rather than closing.

Why it matters here: 8 of the 19 species are weighted 100% to r50to150 and most
of the rest are 0.8 deep, so the community experiences close to the deep rate
(+0.398 °C/dec mean across species over 1993–2023). The layer the model
under-warms is the layer the fish occupy, which biases any temperature
attribution downward. The 2012 step change is also absent from a near-linear
forcing.

Fixing it requires a **time-resolved** observational reference in place of (or
alongside) the WOA climatology — see the methods note in the project README.
Do not attempt to repair it by adjusting the WOA offsets; the offsets are not
the problem.

**Inputs:**
- GFDL thetao monthly zarr store (1961–2010) — still needed for the raw
  time series the bias gets applied to (the climatology files alone don't
  contain a time series)

**Outputs:**

- Annual bias-corrected temperature, wide format (CSV: year × depth)

## Configuration

```{r config}
# ---- Paths (defined ONCE here -- do not redefine in later chunks) -----------
# Parent folder holding one sub-folder per depth, each with a GFDL + WOA
# climatology parquet file
bias_corrected_dir <- "Gfdl_temp forcing/isimip_3a"
# Raw GFDL-MOM6-COBALT2 monthly thetao, 1961-2010 (zarr store)
gfdl_zarr   <- paste0("Gfdl_temp forcing/gfdl-mom6-cobalt2_obsclim_thetao_",
                      "15arcmin_eastern-scotian-shelf_monthly_1961_2010.zarr/")
# isimip_file <- "Gfdl_temp forcing/isimip_3b/gfdl-esm4_r1i1p1f1_ssp585_thetao_60arcmin_eastern-scotian-shelf_mean-year_2015_2100.csv"
out_dir     <- "Gfdl_temp forcing"   # where output CSVs are written
out_prefix  <- "gfdl_temp"           # filename prefix for every output

# ---- Depths ------------------------------------------------------------------
# WOA depth labels (m). GFDL's 32.25 m layer is matched to WOA's 32.5 m, and
# the WOA value is used as the label from here on.
target_depths <- c(2.50, 10.00, 20.00, 32.50, 51.25, 75.00,
                   100.00, 125.00, 156.25)

# Bias reference period: baked into the pre-computed climatology files (1981-2010)
# ref_start <- 1981L
# ref_end   <- 2010L

# ---- Splice / post-2010 extension (NOT used in this script) -----------------
# Belongs with the script that builds Ocean_temp_by_Depth_1961_2100.csv.
# gap_years <- 2011:2014    # gap between GFDL (ends 2010) and ISIMIP (starts 2015)
#
# temp_source "isimip3b": splice ISIMIP3b SSP585 (2015-2100) with a single-year
#   delta, bias = GFDL(2010) - ISIMIP(2015); 2010-2015 come out as six identical
#   years. Keep for FishMIP 3a submissions (evaluation period ends 2010).
# temp_source "glorys":   extend with Copernicus GLORYS12V1 (1993-present);
#   overlaps obsclim 1993-2010 so the delta is a multi-year climatological mean
#   difference per depth and month; resolves the ~2012 regime shift (Zhai et al.
#   2025, State Planet 6-osr9/5). Use for Paper 2 (1961-2024). Physics only --
#   resource forcing still comes from obsclim + ISIMIP3b.
#
# temp_source    <- "isimip3b"          # "isimip3b" | "glorys"
# glorys_file    <- "Gfdl_temp forcing/glorys/glorys12v1_thetao_eastern-scotian-shelf_monthly_1993_2024.csv"
# glorys_from    <- 2011L               # first year taken FROM GLORYS
# overlap_years  <- 1993:2010           # years used to estimate the delta
# glorys_match_m <- 10                  # max GLORYS-to-target depth difference (m)

# ---- Other settings ----------------------------------------------------------
month_levels   <- month.name    # January ... December; fixes month ordering
min_months     <- 12L           # months required for a valid annual mean
depth_tol      <- 1e-6          # tolerance for exact depth matching
depth_match_m  <- 0.5           # max GFDL-to-WOA depth difference when pairing (m)
fill_threshold <- 1e10          # |values| above this are treated as fill/missing

# save_plots <- FALSE           # no plots are made in this file

# Create the output folder if it doesn't exist yet
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# cos(latitude)-weighted mean: cells at higher latitude cover less area.
# NA values (or NA latitudes) are dropped before averaging; if nothing is
# left, returns NA rather than erroring.
wmean <- function(x, lat) {
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(lat)
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  weighted.mean(x[ok], w = cos(lat[ok] * pi / 180))
}

# Convert month numbers (1-12) or month names to an ordered factor, so that
# months sort January -> December instead of alphabetically. Stops with a
# clear message if any value can't be matched, which would otherwise silently
# become NA and break the join between bias and GFDL.
to_month_factor <- function(x, levels = month.name) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) x <- month.name[x]
  f <- factor(as.character(x), levels = levels)
  if (anyNA(f) && !anyNA(x)) {
    stop("Could not match `month` values to month names: ",
         paste(head(base::unique(as.character(x)), 5), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  f
}

# Convert the zarr numeric time axis to Dates using the store's own metadata.
# Reads the "units" attribute (e.g. "days since 1961-01-01") from .zattrs;
# falls back to days since `default_origin` if it can't be parsed.
get_dates <- function(path, time_vals, default_origin = "1961-01-01") {
  attrs <- list()
  f <- file.path(path, "time", ".zattrs")
  if (file.exists(f) && requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)) {
    attrs <- tryCatch(jsonlite::read_json(f), error = function(e) list())
  }
  units <- if (is.null(attrs$units)) "" else as.character(attrs$units)
  # Pull out the unit (days/hours/seconds) and the origin date
  m <- regmatches(units, regexec("^(days|hours|seconds) since ([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2})", units))[[1]]
  if (length(m) == 4) {
    origin  <- as.Date(m[4])
    divisor <- c(days = 1, hours = 24, seconds = 86400)[[m[2]]]  # -> days
  } else {
    message("Could not read time units from .zattrs; assuming days since ", default_origin)
    origin  <- as.Date(default_origin)
    divisor <- 1
  }
  # as.Date() assumes a Gregorian calendar; warn if the store says otherwise
  cal <- attrs$calendar
  if (!is.null(cal) &&
      !tolower(as.character(cal)) %in% c("standard", "gregorian", "proleptic_gregorian")) {
    warning("Time calendar is '", cal, "', not Gregorian; dates built with as.Date() can drift.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  origin + floor(time_vals / divisor)
}
```

# 1. Bias: pre-extracted per-depth WOA + GFDL climatologies

## 1.1 Locate and validate depth folders

```{r depth-folder-check}
# One sub-folder per depth, e.g. "2.5_gfdl_woa-regridded_bias-corr-data_..."
depth_folders <- list.dirs(bias_corrected_dir, recursive = FALSE, full.names = TRUE)
if (length(depth_folders) == 0) {
  stop("No depth folders found under ", bias_corrected_dir, call. = FALSE)
}

# The depth in metres is the leading number of each folder name
depth_vals <- as.numeric(sub("^([0-9.]+)_.*$", "\\1", basename(depth_folders)))
if (anyNA(depth_vals)) {
  stop("Could not parse a depth value from folder name(s): ",
       paste(basename(depth_folders)[is.na(depth_vals)], collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}

# Each folder must contain exactly ONE GFDL and ONE WOA climatology file;
# anything else means the wrong file could be picked up silently later.
file_counts <- sapply(depth_folders, function(p) {
  f <- list.files(p)
  c(gfdl = sum(grepl("obsclim_thetao.*mthly_clim_mean", f)),
    woa  = sum(grepl("regridded_woa", f)))
})
colnames(file_counts) <- basename(depth_folders)
print(t(file_counts))

if (any(file_counts != 1)) {
  stop("Some depth folders don't have exactly one GFDL + one WOA climatology file -- ",
       "check the printout above.", call. = FALSE)
}

message("Found ", length(depth_folders), " depth folders: ",
        paste(base::sort(depth_vals), collapse = ", "))
```

## 1.2 Regional monthly bias per depth

```{r monthly-bias}
# For one depth folder: read the GFDL and WOA climatologies, collapse each from
# a lat/lon grid to a single cos-lat weighted regional mean per calendar month,
# and return them side by side.
read_clim_pair <- function(path, depth) {
  files <- list.files(path, full.names = TRUE)

  gfdl_file <- files[grepl("obsclim_thetao.*mthly_clim_mean", files)][1]
  woa_file  <- files[grepl("regridded_woa", basename(files))][1]

  gfdl_df <- read_parquet(gfdl_file) %>% select(lat, lon, month, vals)
  woa_df  <- read_parquet(woa_file)  %>% select(lat, lon, month, vals)

  # GFDL 1981-2010 climatology -> one regional mean per calendar month
  gfdl_monthly <- gfdl_df %>%
    mutate(month = to_month_factor(month, month_levels)) %>%
    group_by(month) %>%
    summarise(gfdl_ref_mean = wmean(vals, lat), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(depth = depth)

  # WOA climatology (already regridded to the GFDL grid) -> same treatment
  woa_monthly_d <- woa_df %>%
    mutate(month = to_month_factor(month, month_levels)) %>%
    group_by(month) %>%
    summarise(woa_mean = wmean(vals, lat), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(depth = depth)

  inner_join(woa_monthly_d, gfdl_monthly, by = c("depth", "month"))
}

# Loop over all depths, stack, and compute the additive bias.
# Positive bias = GFDL is too cold, so the correction warms it.
monthly_bias_all <- map2_dfr(depth_folders, depth_vals, read_clim_pair) %>%
  mutate(bias = woa_mean - gfdl_ref_mean) %>%
  arrange(depth, month)

print(monthly_bias_all, n = Inf)

# Sanity checks: no missing bias values, and 9 depths x 12 months = 108 rows
if (anyNA(monthly_bias_all$bias)) {
  stop("monthly_bias_all has NA bias values -- check depth folder contents.", call. = FALSE)
}
message("monthly_bias_all rows: ", nrow(monthly_bias_all),
        " (expect ", length(depth_folders) * 12, ")")
```

# 2. GFDL: raw monthly series (1961–2010) from the zarr store

The climatology files above only cover 1981–2010 and contain no time
series -- the bias still needs to be applied to GFDL's actual monthly
values across the full 1961–2010 record.

```{r gfdl-build-fn}
# Read one variable from the zarr store and return a long data frame
# (date, depth, lat, lon, value), keeping only the target depths and
# dropping missing cells.
build_var_df <- function(path, varname, depths = target_depths,
                         tol = depth_tol, match_m = depth_match_m) {
  # Strip any trailing slash, then check the store and the variable exist
  path <- sub("[/\\\\]+$", "", path)
  if (!dir.exists(path)) {
    stop("Zarr store not found: ", path, "\n(working directory: ", getwd(), ")", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(path, varname))) {
    stop("No array called '", varname, "' in the store. Found: ",
         paste(list.files(path, all.files = FALSE), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }

  # Coordinate axes and the data array
  depth_bin <- as.vector(read_zarr_array(file.path(path, "depth_bin_m")))
  lat       <- as.vector(read_zarr_array(file.path(path, "lat")))
  lon       <- as.vector(read_zarr_array(file.path(path, "lon")))
  time_vals <- as.vector(read_zarr_array(file.path(path, "time")))
  var_arr   <- read_zarr_array(file.path(path, varname))

  # The array must be [time, depth, lat, lon]. Some zarr readers return the
  # dimensions reversed, so transpose if that is what we got.
  expected <- c(length(time_vals), length(depth_bin), length(lat), length(lon))
  dims     <- dim(var_arr)
  if (identical(as.integer(dims), base::rev(as.integer(expected)))) {
    var_arr <- aperm(var_arr)
    dims    <- dim(var_arr)
  }
  if (!identical(as.integer(dims), as.integer(expected))) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "Dimension mismatch for %s: array dims = %s, expected [time,depth,lat,lon] = %s",
      varname, paste(dims, collapse = "x"), paste(expected, collapse = "x")
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }

  message("GFDL depth_bin_m values in store: ", paste(depth_bin, collapse = ", "))

  # Pair each GFDL depth with its nearest WOA target depth, and keep it only
  # if it is within `match_m` metres (e.g. GFDL 32.25 -> WOA 32.5).
  nearest_idx <- vapply(depth_bin, function(z) base::which.min(abs(depths - z)), integer(1))
  keep        <- which(abs(depth_bin - depths[nearest_idx]) <= match_m)
  if (length(keep) == 0) {
    stop("None of the target depths match depth_bin_m within ", match_m, " m.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # Relabel kept GFDL depths with the WOA depth, and report any that changed
  new_labels <- depths[nearest_idx[keep]]
  changed <- abs(depth_bin[keep] - new_labels) > tol
  if (any(changed)) {
    message(paste(sprintf("  Matching GFDL depth %.2f -> WOA depth %.2f",
                          depth_bin[keep][changed], new_labels[changed]),
                  collapse = "\n"))
  }
  # Two GFDL layers collapsing onto one WOA depth would double-count it
  if (anyDuplicated(new_labels)) {
    stop("Two GFDL depths matched the same WOA depth: ",
         paste(new_labels[duplicated(new_labels)], collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }

  # Subset the array to the kept depths and apply the new labels
  var_arr   <- var_arr[, keep, , , drop = FALSE]
  depth_bin <- new_labels

  # Huge values are fill/missing markers, not real temperatures
  var_arr[!is.na(var_arr) & abs(var_arr) > fill_threshold] <- NA

  dates <- get_dates(path, time_vals)
  message(sprintf("  %s: %d time steps, %s to %s", varname, length(dates), min(dates), max(dates)))

  # Flatten the 4-D array to long format. expand.grid varies its first factor
  # fastest, matching R's column-major order for [time, depth, lat, lon], so
  # as.vector(var_arr) lines up row for row.
  df <- expand.grid(
    time_idx    = seq_along(time_vals),
    depth_bin_m = depth_bin,
    lat         = lat, lon         = lon,
    KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE)
  df$date       <- dates[df$time_idx]
  df$time_idx   <- NULL
  df[[varname]] <- as.vector(var_arr)
  df[!is.na(df[[varname]]), , drop = FALSE]   # drop land / missing cells
}

thetao_df <- build_var_df(gfdl_zarr, "thetao")
```

```{r gfdl-monthly}
# Collapse the grid to one cos-lat weighted regional mean per depth x month,
# then add year and calendar-month columns (month as an ordered factor so it
# joins cleanly to the bias table).
gfdl_monthly_all <- thetao_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(thetao)) %>%
  group_by(depth_bin_m, date) %>%
  summarise(vals = wmean(thetao, lat), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::rename(depth = depth_bin_m) %>%
  mutate(
    year  = as.integer(format(date, "%Y")),
    month = to_month_factor(as.integer(format(date, "%m")), month_levels)
  ) %>%
  arrange(depth, year, month)

# The gridded data frame is large; free it now that the regional means exist
rm(thetao_df); invisible(base::gc())

message(sprintf("GFDL monthly series: %d rows across %d depths, %d to %d",
                nrow(gfdl_monthly_all), n_distinct(gfdl_monthly_all$depth),
                min(gfdl_monthly_all$year), max(gfdl_monthly_all$year)))
```

## 2.1 Depth-alignment check (raw GFDL vs bias table depths)

```{r depth-check}
# The join in section 3 matches on depth, so the depth labels must agree
# between the raw GFDL series and the bias table.
gfdl_depths <- base::sort(base::unique(gfdl_monthly_all$depth))
bias_depths <- base::sort(base::unique(monthly_bias_all$depth))
message("GFDL depths (after matching): ", paste(gfdl_depths, collapse = ", "))
message("Bias table depths:            ", paste(bias_depths, collapse = ", "))

# Any GFDL depth with no bias counterpart would be silently dropped by the
# inner_join, so flag it here.
unmatched <- gfdl_depths[
  vapply(gfdl_depths, function(d) !any(abs(bias_depths - d) < depth_tol), logical(1))
]
if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
  warning("GFDL depth(s) with no bias-table counterpart: ", paste(unmatched, collapse = ", "),
          " -- they will be dropped from the correction.")
} else {
  message("All GFDL depths align with the bias table.")
}
```

# 3. Apply the bias and aggregate to annual means

```{r apply-bias}
# Add the depth x calendar-month offset to every monthly value. The same
# offset is used in every year, so the interannual variability and trend of
# GFDL are unchanged (see LIMITATION above).
gfdl_corrected_all <- gfdl_monthly_all %>%
  inner_join(monthly_bias_all %>% select(depth, month, bias), by = c("depth", "month")) %>%
  mutate(vals_corrected = vals + bias) %>%
  arrange(depth, year, month)
```

```{r annual-means}
# Annual mean per depth. A year only counts if all 12 months are present;
# otherwise the mean would be biased by the missing season, so set to NA.
# raw_annual is kept alongside for raw-vs-corrected comparison.
gfdl_annual_all <- gfdl_corrected_all %>%
  group_by(depth, year) %>%
  summarise(n_months         = sum(!is.na(vals_corrected)),
            raw_annual       = mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
            corrected_annual = mean(vals_corrected, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(raw_annual       = if_else(n_months >= min_months, raw_annual, NA_real_),
         corrected_annual = if_else(n_months >= min_months, corrected_annual, NA_real_))
```

```{r annual-wide}
# Reshape to one row per year and one column per depth (Depth_2.5, Depth_10, ...)
gfdl_annual_wide <- gfdl_annual_all %>%
  select(depth, year, corrected_annual) %>%
  arrange(depth, year) %>%            # keeps columns in depth order
  pivot_wider(names_from = depth, values_from = corrected_annual, names_prefix = "Depth_") %>%
  arrange(year)

print(gfdl_annual_wide)
```

# 5. Plot the output

Plots of the saved output: raw vs. bias-corrected annual temperature at each
depth, and the monthly bias that was applied. With `save_plots <- TRUE` both
are also written to `out_dir`.

```{r plot-annual, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# Long format: one row per depth x year x series (raw / corrected).
# Depth becomes an ordered factor so panels run shallow -> deep.
plot_annual <- gfdl_annual_all %>%
  select(depth, year, raw = raw_annual, corrected = corrected_annual) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(raw, corrected), names_to = "series", values_to = "temp") %>%
  mutate(series = factor(series, levels = c("raw", "corrected"),
                         labels = c("GFDL raw", "GFDL bias-corrected")),
         depth_lab = factor(paste0(depth, " m"),
                            levels = paste0(base::sort(base::unique(depth)), " m")))

p_annual <- ggplot(plot_annual, aes(year, temp, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ depth_lab, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +   # own y-range per depth
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("GFDL raw" = "grey50",
                                 "GFDL bias-corrected" = "firebrick")) +
  labs(title = "Annual mean temperature, Eastern Scotian Shelf (1961-2010)",
       subtitle = "Constant monthly offset: levels shift, trend and variability are unchanged",
       x = NULL, y = "Temperature (\u00b0C)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_annual)

```


TWO layers, which is what the code has always produced despite the heading
previously saying three:

- `r0to50`   = 2.5 / 10 / 20 / 32.5 m
- `r50to150` = 51.25 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 156.25 m

The second was labelled `r50to100` while actually spanning 51–156 m. Renamed to
`r50to150`, which is what the committed CSV already carried and what
`03.Realms setup.Rmd` and `05.Thermizer_runs.Rmd` expect. The names matter
beyond cosmetics only in one direction: therMizer matches `ocean_temp` columns
to realms **by position**, so a disagreement here would not error, it would
silently pair the wrong temperature with the wrong stratum.

Known limitation, see the note in the Overview: in July, when the water column
is stratified, the warming is confined to the top 10 m (+0.325 °C/dec at 2.5 m,
+0.219 at 10 m, nothing at 20–32.5 m). Averaging those four levels dilutes it to
+0.128. Finer strata would preserve the signal; the Hawaii longline therMizer
model uses 18 depth ranges keyed to species' preferred depths for this reason.

```{r combine-layers}
combined_wide_layers <- gfdl_annual_wide %>%
  mutate(r0to50 = rowMeans(across(c(Depth_2.5, Depth_10, Depth_20, Depth_32.5)),
         na.rm = TRUE),
    r50to150 = rowMeans(across(c(Depth_51.25, Depth_75, Depth_100, Depth_125, Depth_156.25)),
                        na.rm = TRUE) ) %>% select(year, r0to50, r50to150)

print(combined_wide_layers)
write.csv(combined_wide_layers, "Temp_by depth.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create the output folder if it doesn't exist
dir.create(save_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Save as CSV
write.csv(
  combined_wide_layers,
  file.path(save_dir, "Temp_by depth.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
